anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: The paper describes MNE-BIDS, a general framework and tool for organizing and analyzing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format, not the specific dataset on007169.

anchors.paper_title: EEG-BIDS, an extension to the brain imaging data structure for electroencephalography
anchors.reason: The paper introduces EEG-BIDS, an extension to the BIDS standard, which is a technical specification/tool for organizing EEG data, not a paper describing the specific cognitive workload dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Data were collected using a combined EEG+ECG mobile system (19-channel 10-20 montage, Ag/AgCl electrodes, linked-ear reference, 250 Hz sampling) and Pupil Labs Pupil Core eye tracker, synchronized via Lab Streaming Layer. The n-back protocol included a tutorial phase (20 trials per difficulty level with feedback) followed by a main experiment (100 trials per level without feedback). Each trial presented a letter for 1.0 s followed by a 0.7 s blank interval. Original recordings in XDF format were converted to BIDS with EEG in BrainVision format, pupil data exported as TSV files, and task events aligned to EEG start time.
